zh.title: Simple Flying於范保羅航展導覽阿聯酋航空空中巴士A350客艙
zh.summary: Simple Flying團隊於2026年范保羅航展期間，實地導覽阿聯酋航空全新空中巴士A350-900寬體客機。導覽涵蓋該航空公司全新的商務艙、擴大設置的豪華經濟艙、升級的ice機上娛樂系統，以及重新設計的經濟艙，展示各客艙配備與乘客搭乘體驗。
body: 在2026年范保羅航展期間，Simple Flying團隊的Tom與Alejandro對阿聯酋航空最新的空中巴士A350-900寬體客機進行了全面導覽，實地檢視該機型的內部客艙配置。
本次導覽涵蓋阿聯酋航空全新的商務艙與擴增的豪華經濟艙，同時展示升級後的ice機上娛樂系統，以及重新設計的經濟艙設施。
導覽團隊深入探訪各個客艙區域，重點介紹該款新一代寬體客機的各項最新功能與配備，呈現旅客未來搭乘阿聯酋航空最新機型時可期待的設施與服務體驗。

en.title: Simple Flying Tours Emirates' New Airbus A350-900 at Farnborough Airshow 2026
en.summary: Tom and Alejandro of Simple Flying conducted a full tour of Emirates' brand-new Airbus A350-900 aircraft during the Farnborough Airshow 2026. Their walkthrough detailed the interior cabin features across all classes, including the airline's all-new Business Class, an expanded Premium Economy cabin, an upgraded ice inflight entertainment system, and a redesigned Economy Class. The tour provided a detailed overview of every cabin, highlighting the latest features and showing what passengers can expect when flying on the carrier's newest widebody aircraft.
body: Tom and Alejandro of Simple Flying took a full tour of Emirates' brand-new Airbus A350-900 widebody aircraft during the Farnborough Airshow 2026, providing a detailed look inside the jet's interior.

The cabin tour highlighted the airline's all-new Business Class seating and an expanded Premium Economy cabin. The presentation also showcased the upgraded ice inflight entertainment system alongside a newly redesigned Economy Class.

By exploring every cabin throughout the aircraft, the walkthrough highlighted the widebody's latest features and provided a closer look at what passengers can expect when flying on Emirates' newest fleet addition.

zh.title: 日本航空攜手日立與商船三井 於沖繩久米島展開直接海洋碳捕捉測試
zh.summary: 日本航空於2026年8月4日宣布，已與日立及商船三井簽署協議，將於沖繩縣久米島共同進行日本首個直接海洋碳捕捉技術的實證測試。該項目將利用設置於陸地上的貨櫃化設備抽取海水並分離二氧化碳。日本航空亦與區域夥伴日本越洋航空及琉球空中通勤合作推廣該計畫，並探索未來將捕捉到的二氧化碳作為製造永續航空燃料原料的可行性。
body: 日本航空（Japan Airlines, JAL）於2026年8月4日宣布，已與日立製作所（Hitachi）及商船三井（Mitsui O.S.K. Lines, MOL）簽署合作協議，將共同於沖繩縣久米島啟動日本首個直接海洋碳捕捉（Direct Ocean Capture）技術的試驗計畫。這項技術旨在直接從海水中提取溶解的二氧化碳，藉此降低大氣中的溫室氣體濃度。
根據三家公司公布的試驗方案，計畫將於沖繩縣久米島的陸地上設置貨櫃化設備。該設備將吸入當地海水並分離抽取其中的二氧化碳，隨後將處理過的海水排放回海洋。試驗的主要目的在於評估該技術在使用真實海水環境下的運轉效率，同時收集有關營運挑戰與環境影響的實務資料，為未來在日本沿海地區的推廣應用提供依據。
參與該項目的三家企業先前均已投資總部位於美國的海洋碳捕捉技術開發商 Captura Corp.，並持續探討將相關技術引進日本的可行性。在此次試驗中，各公司分工明確：日立將運用其分析工具進行技術監測，追蹤水質與營運資料，以確定最具能源效率的運轉方式，並計畫建置資料平台以驗證實際捕捉的碳量；商船三井則利用與當地政府的合作關係，負責協調居民溝通與試驗場地建置。
在航空業務與社會溝通方面，日本航空將與旗下已營運久米島航線的區域航空公司日本越洋航空（Japan Transocean Air）及琉球空中通勤（Ryukyu Air Commuter）合作，主導該計畫的外界溝通與公眾宣導工作。此外，日本航空亦著眼於長期效益，規劃探索將捕捉到的二氧化碳轉化為生產永續航空燃料（SAF）原始原料的可行性。
選擇久米島作為實證測試場地，主要原因之一在於該島已具備其他海洋能源研究基礎，包括利用海水溫差發電的系統設施。試驗團隊指出，海水所含二氧化碳濃度約為空氣的100至150倍，直接海洋碳捕捉被視為比直接大氣捕捉更具成本效益與低能耗的去碳途徑。

en.title: Japan Airlines Partners with Hitachi and MOL for Ocean Carbon Capture Test on Kume Island
en.summary: Japan Airlines announced on August 4, 2026, that it has partnered with Hitachi and Mitsui O.S.K. Lines to conduct Japan's first pilot test of Direct Ocean Capture technology on Kume Island in Okinawa Prefecture. The project will deploy land-based containerized equipment to draw in seawater and remove dissolved carbon dioxide. Japan Airlines, alongside regional partners Japan Transocean Air and Ryukyu Air Commuter, will lead outreach efforts for the test and aims to explore utilizing the captured carbon dioxide as a raw material to produce sustainable aviation fuel in the long term.
body: Japan Airlines announced on August 4, 2026, that it has signed an agreement with Hitachi and Mitsui O.S.K. Lines to conduct Japan's first pilot test of Direct Ocean Capture technology on Kume Island in Okinawa Prefecture. The joint project aims to extract carbon dioxide directly dissolved in seawater to support atmospheric decarbonization efforts.

Under the trial plan, the companies will install land-based containerized equipment on Kume Island to draw in local seawater, strip out dissolved carbon dioxide, and release the processed water back into the ocean. The pilot is designed to evaluate the technology's performance under real-world ocean conditions while gathering practical operational and environmental data to guide potential future deployments along Japan's coastline.

All three companies have previously invested in Captura Corp., a United States-based ocean carbon capture technology developer, and have spent time exploring options to deploy the technology in Japan. Within the project framework, Hitachi will oversee technical monitoring using analytical tools to track water quality and operational metrics, while developing a data platform to verify captured carbon for potential carbon credit trading.

Mitsui O.S.K. Lines will leverage its existing relationship with the local government on Kume Island to coordinate with residents and construct the pilot site. Meanwhile, Japan Airlines, working alongside regional partner carriers Japan Transocean Air and Ryukyu Air Commuter that currently operate flights to Kumejima, will lead community outreach and public awareness efforts for the project.

Kume Island was selected as the pilot location in part because it already hosts ocean-based energy research infrastructure, including a system that generates electricity from ocean temperature differences. Because seawater holds roughly 100 to 150 times more concentrated carbon dioxide than atmospheric air, ocean capture is viewed as a potentially less energy-intensive and lower-cost approach to emissions offset. Over the long term, Japan Airlines plans to explore utilizing the captured carbon dioxide as a raw material to produce sustainable aviation fuel.
